plan.title: Gradient descent: two learning rates on the same bowl
plan.description: A long, narrow bowl-shaped loss surface shows two balls, one blue and one orange, starting at the same point. Each ball takes downhill gradient-descent steps with its own learning rate and leaves a trail. You can see that a small rate creeps slowly toward the bottom, a larger rate zigzags across the steep walls, and a rate that is too large makes the ball bounce higher until it leaves the surface. Readouts show the step count and each ball's current loss.
plan.reason: Running both learning rates side by side on the same surface, from the same start, makes the difference easy to see: you watch the speed, the zigzag or the divergence happen step by step, and you can change either rate and run it again.
interactions: Change the blue ball's learning rate: its step length changes, so its trail gets denser or sparser and its loss falls more slowly or more quickly
Change the orange ball's rate: below 0.25 it slides smoothly, between 0.25 and 0.5 it zigzags but still reaches the bottom, above 0.5 the zigzag grows until it leaves the surface
Play, pause or step the run: each step moves both balls once and adds a point to each trail
Restart both runs: both balls go back to the start and their trails clear, but your two learning rates are kept
Orbit the camera to view the trails from above or from the side
assumptions: Illustration: a simple made-up bowl, not a loss from a real trained model.
The loss is half of (x squared plus 4 times y squared), so the bowl is four times steeper in the y direction than in the x direction. The lowest point is at the centre, where the loss is 0.

Each step moves a ball against the gradient (the direction of steepest uphill): x becomes x minus rate times x, and y becomes y minus rate times 4y. The gradient is computed exactly, with no noise and no momentum.
Both balls start at x = -3, y = 1.5, where the loss is 9.
A run ends after 60 steps. A ball also stops early when its loss drops below 0.001 (marked 'converged') or when it moves outside the drawn surface (marked 'diverged').
limitations: On this exact bowl, any rate above 0.5 diverges and any rate below it converges. Real losses are not perfect bowls, so the safe range there is different and usually unknown in advance.
A ball that diverges is stopped at the edge of the surface so the scene stays readable. It does not keep flying away.
Only plain gradient descent is shown. Momentum, adaptive methods and random mini-batch noise are left out.
plan.learningGoal: See how the learning rate sets the step size in gradient descent. Too small is slow, a moderate rate can zigzag across steep directions, and too large makes the loss grow instead of shrink.

draft.title: Gradient descent: two learning rates on the same bowl
draft.description: A long, narrow bowl-shaped loss surface, drawn with contour lines. A blue ball and an orange ball start at the same point on the bowl's side, drawn side by side. Each step, each ball moves downhill against the gradient with its own learning rate and adds a point to its trail. A small rate creeps slowly toward the lowest point. A larger rate zigzags across the steep walls. A rate above 0.5 swings higher each step until the ball leaves the surface. Readouts show each ball's loss, the step count and each ball's status.
assumptions: Illustration: a simple made-up bowl, not a loss from a real trained model.

Loss = (x² + 4y²)/2, so the bowl is 4 times steeper along y (drawn left to right on screen) than along x. The lowest point is the centre, loss 0. The surface is drawn at 0.1 × loss over x, y from −4 to 4.
Each step: x ← x − rate·x, y ← y − rate·4y, with the exact gradient (no noise, no momentum). Both balls start at x = −3, y = 1.5, where the loss is 9. The run takes 5 steps a second.

A run ends after 60 steps. A ball stops early when its loss drops below 0.001 (converged) or when it leaves the drawn square |x|, |y| ≤ 4 (diverged). On this bowl any rate above 0.5 diverges and any rate below it converges.
A diverged ball is drawn held at the edge of the surface, but its Loss readout shows the true value. Changing either learning rate starts both runs again from the start, with the trails cleared.
When both balls are at the same point (at the start, or both at the bottom), they are drawn 0.2 to either side along x so both stay visible; the trails show the exact positions.

previousDraft.description: A long, narrow bowl-shaped loss surface, drawn with contour lines. A blue ball and an orange ball start at the same point on the bowl's side, drawn side by side. Each step, each ball moves downhill against the gradient with its own learning rate and adds a point to its trail. A small rate creeps slowly toward the lowest point. A larger rate zigzags across the steep walls. A rate above 0.5 swings higher each step until the ball leaves the surface. Readouts show each ball's loss, the step count and each ball's status.
assumptions: Illustration: a simple made-up bowl, not a loss from a real trained model.

Loss = (x² + 4y²)/2, so the bowl is 4 times steeper along y (drawn left to right on screen) than along x. The lowest point is the centre, loss 0. The surface is drawn at 0.1 × loss over x, y from −4 to 4.
Each step: x ← x − rate·x, y ← y − rate·4y, with the exact gradient (no noise, no momentum). Both balls start at x = −3, y = 1.5, where the loss is 9. The run takes 5 steps a second.

A run ends after 60 steps. A ball stops early when its loss drops below 0.001 (converged) or when it leaves the drawn square |x|, |y| ≤ 4 (diverged). On this bowl any rate above 0.5 diverges and any rate below it converges.
A diverged ball is drawn held at the edge of the surface, but its Loss readout shows the true value. Changing either learning rate starts both runs again from the start, with the trails cleared.
When both balls are at the same point (at the start, or both at the bottom), they are drawn 0.2 to either side along x so both stay visible; the trails show the exact positions.

blocks.text:
I wrote the missing behavior program and left the rest of the artifact unchanged.

- **Stepping:** each step moves both balls once using the plan's rule: x becomes x − rate·x and y becomes y − rate·4y. The loss is (x² + 4y²)/2. Both balls start at x = −3, y = 1.5. The run takes 5 steps a second (one every 6 of the host's ticks), and "Step once" moves them exactly once.
- **Stopping:** a ball stops when its loss drops below 0.001 ("converged") or when it leaves the square |x|, |y| ≤ 4 ("diverged"). The whole run stops after 60 steps, or earlier once both balls have stopped. A diverged ball is drawn at the edge of the surface, but its loss readout shows the true value.
- **Picture and numbers:** each trail gains one point per step. When the two balls are at the same point they are drawn 0.2 to either side so both stay visible. The losses, step count and status words come from the same positions that move the balls.
- **Controls:** "Restart both runs, keep rates" sends both balls back to the start, clears the trails and keeps your rates. Changing either rate also restarts both runs. Pressing Run after a run has finished starts a new one.

I'm passing all six captures. I found no blocker or major problem, and I'm reporting two minor findings.

**Numbers check out.** I worked the step formulas by hand at the sampled settings, and every readout matches:
- **Blue rate 0.08 and orange rate 0.45, 14 steps:** blue loss is 0.4359 and orange loss is 0.0087.
- **Blue rate 0.6:** the blue ball leaves the surface on step 3 with a true loss of 33.90. Its trail has 4 points, and the ball is held at the edge, as the assumptions say.
- **Step count:** 48 host ticks at one step per 6 ticks give 8 steps. Step once adds 1 and 30 more ticks add 5, which makes 14.

**The behaviour matches the plan.** Both controls, their ranges, steps and defaults (0.05 and 0.45), the start point, the loss of 9, the 60-step limit and the 0.001 cutoff all match the request and plan exactly. The pictures agree with the readouts: blue creeps along a smooth curve, orange zigzags across the steep direction and reaches the bottom, and blue at 0.6 swings wider each step until it reaches the edge.

**The scene is readable.** The bowl fills the default view, the colours are clear and the trails are thick enough to see. The first control is the blue ball's rate and the first readout is the blue ball's loss.

**Minor findings:**
- **Label crowding:** the "Lowest point" label sits right next to where the orange ball and the end of its zigzag gather, which is a little crowded. It does not cover either ball. This can be fixed.
- **Not sampled:** no capture changed the orange rate, and no capture used either rate at its lowest value, 0.01. The orange ball's three behaviours the plan promises (smooth below 0.25, zigzag but converging up to 0.5, diverging above 0.5) are therefore checked only from the program, not from a render.
